A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PoSh and DOCENT. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original DOCENT annotations, metric evaluations on DOCENT and CapArena, and human comparisons of supervised and PoSh-reward training.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds manual evaluations of PoSh's components, DSG baseline results and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3, model choices, extraction and question-templating pseudocode, and prompts retain the same procedure. Newly described inference optimizations and revised scores do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use DOCENT artwork, CapArena web imagery, the same complex multi-person subset, and DOCENT description training and evaluation. The new component audits sample existing DOCENT coverage without introducing another domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds Davidsonian Scene Graph (DSG) as an evaluated image-based baseline on DOCENT. v1 cited DSG but did not report this comparison. Existing granular and coarse comparators and the SFT comparison are retained.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.4.2 introduces evaluation against ten manually annotated descriptions, split into five references and five generations, and 620 verification questions from two randomly sampled pairs. It specifies element precision/recall/F1, attachment accuracies and threshold-swept verification F1. Existing benchmark and training protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds separate manual validation of both central pipeline stages: scene-graph extraction and element verification, including coreference and attachment accuracy (A.4.2, Tables 8–9). It also adds runtime analysis against DCScore. These introduce a substantial new layer of component reliability and efficiency analysis beyond v1's retained benchmark and robustness evaluations.

E5.justification: Table 6 now explicitly shades nonsignificant correlations for retained baselines including BLEU-4, FLEUR and Prometheus. v1's caption declared the same alpha = 0.05 convention but its table lacked these markings. This expands explicit significance reporting; no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or statistical testing procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Results are substantially revised and extended. Table 2 changes PoSh mistake F1 from 0.559 to 0.580 and 4GramEmbed omission F1 from 0.505 to 0.641. Tables 3/6 revise PoSh's coarse scores; Table 4 changes GPT4o reference coverage from 0.437 to 0.501. PoSh's multi-person CapArena correlations change from rho/tau = 0.776/0.648 to 0.727/0.581. DSG, component-quality and runtime results are newly reported. The PDFs do not explain the revisions to existing scores.

T1.justification: The scene-graph definitions and granular/coarse scoring equations in Section 3 are unchanged. The new component evaluations introduce empirical measurements, with no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introductory contributions and conclusion retain the claims about PoSh's interpretability, reproducibility, human alignment, robustness and reward usefulness, together with DOCENT and its artwork-description task. New diagnostics and timing evidence support these existing claims.

C2.justification: New Section 9 identifies untested potential bias toward models using structural priors. A.4.2 attributes verification errors to reference omissions, interpretive language and identifier-templating limitations. Section 6 additionally discusses synthetic-description scaling, token-level guidance and the quality–runtime tradeoff.

D1.justification: v2 specifies CUDA 12.8, continuous batching and prefix caching, and reports 400 descriptions scored in 15 minutes on one H100. It updates example-access instructions to a specific public repository location. H100 inference and batch invariance were already disclosed in v1; conversely, v2 removes the statement that SFT/DAPO training used eight H100 GPUs.

R1.justification: New A.1.1 expands the comparison with already-cited DSG, distinguishing reference use, long descriptions, entity collisions and precision versus recall. References add work on inference serving, synthetic descriptions, structural-prior VLMs and token-level guidance, while removing Bloom et al. (2025). The overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds focused discussions, gives the retained leaderboard its own section, introduces a limitations section and reorganizes appendix subsections. It clarifies terminology such as 'PoSh-tuned' for the trained Qwen variant. Most existing exposition remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–9 and a DSG row in Table 6, adjusts table formatting and supplies Table 6's significance shading. Table 2 and several figures move, and appendix instructions and interfaces are regrouped. All nine existing figures retain identical image content.

improvement.justification: The component audits, DSG comparison and runtime evidence make the existing method better supported and easier to assess. v2 also aligns Section 6's granular scores with Table 2 and supplies missing significance markings in Table 6. These gains are limited by the small diagnostic samples and unexplained score revisions, with a modest reproducibility loss from removing the training-hardware disclosure.
